screenshots.title: Account access
screenshots.description: Email/phone credentials, Google sign-in, phone OTP, and password recovery provide entry points to the account-based hazard and family features. The screenshot shows sign-in choices rather than a completed login.

screenshots.title: Hazard dashboard
screenshots.description: Active alerts, earthquake totals, and storm signals summarize current activity. The featured typhoon card and recent earthquake list lead into detailed tracking and event reports.

screenshots.title: Combined hazard map
screenshots.description: Earthquake and typhoon markers share a regional map. Magnitude filters and the color legend help users narrow events and see where activity is concentrated.

screenshots.title: Typhoon track and timeline
screenshots.description: Storm-track points, intensity colors, weather imagery, and a playback timeline let users inspect the storm position over time. The legend distinguishes storm intensity and projected track markers.

screenshots.title: Earthquake event details
screenshots.description: Magnitude, location, depth, distance, and a location-based assessment explain one selected earthquake. Area, sharing, and felt-report actions support follow-up; the displayed assessment is an app estimate, not an official safety determination.

screenshots.title: Earthquake report browser
screenshots.description: Search, severity filters, totals, and sorting organize a list of earthquake reports. Each entry provides magnitude, location, depth, and time before the user opens detailed information.

screenshots.title: Typhoon reports and local weather
screenshots.description: Storm-category filters and signal counts sit above a Philippine weather list. Regional filters and the location card let users move between storm monitoring and local weather conditions.

screenshots.title: Family and friends directory
screenshots.description: Contact cards show activity and location-sharing state alongside communication actions. The directory gathers family connections so the user can choose whom to contact or locate.

screenshots.title: Family circles and live location
screenshots.description: The screen combines a sharing switch, create/join circle actions, a map, and member information. It lets users organize family circles and control their own location-sharing preference.

screenshots.title: Family emergency-alert settings
screenshots.description: A master family-alert switch, auto-SMS and auto-call settings, saved contacts, and test/share shortcuts configure intended emergency communication. Several controls are disabled in the captured state; actual delivery is not demonstrated.

screenshots.title: Notification preferences
screenshots.description: Earthquake, typhoon, flood, sound/vibration, and emergency-override controls appear beneath the profile. Users can select alert categories and open emergency-contact setup.

screenshots.title: Profile and app preferences
screenshots.description: The profile form collects a name, mobile number, and home address. Alert threshold, language, background synchronization, and appearance settings control the wider app experience.

screenshots.title: Appearance and emergency options
screenshots.description: Theme and display-mode choices appear above strobe, SMS-fallback, mesh-relay, and panic-gesture switches. This screen configures optional behaviors; it does not demonstrate successful emergency delivery or nearby relay.

screenshots.title: Help, privacy, and account controls
screenshots.description: Help Center, Data Sources, Privacy Policy, version information, sign-out, and account deletion give users a place to inspect application information and manage their account.

screenshots.title: Sign-in and account entry
screenshots.description: Email/password, Google, and GitHub options lead into the personal study workspace. Password recovery and sign-up links support returning and first-time learners.

screenshots.title: Manual quiz builder
screenshots.description: Creation-mode tabs, a title field, question-count presets, difficulty choices, and question-type buttons define a new quiz. The disabled Save Quiz button reflects a draft with no questions added yet.

screenshots.title: Quiz library empty state
screenshots.description: Search, progress filters, completed-test totals, average score, and study-time metrics frame the quiz library. The empty list shows how the module appears before study sets have been created.

screenshots.title: Learner profile and preferences
screenshots.description: The profile combines identity, flashcard totals, daily streak, and mastery with theme, reminder, password, subscription, and cache controls. It centralizes account settings and study-progress indicators.

screenshots.title: Subscription and trial state
screenshots.description: The plan page compares Free and Pro features and shows a cancelled trial that remains active until the displayed date. It explains the captured account entitlement; displayed prices and dates are historical screenshot content.

screenshots.title: Photo-to-quiz capture
screenshots.description: Camera and image-upload options begin the Scan to Quiz workflow. Capture tips explain how to prepare a clear image before OCR and question parsing; no extracted text is shown yet.

screenshots.title: Bulk-question import guide
screenshots.description: The Bulk Paste mode displays examples for multiple-choice, true/false, identification, and enumeration syntax. The format guide helps users structure pasted questions and mark correct answers before importing.

screenshots.title: Document-based AI setup
screenshots.description: The AI Generate tab accepts a course document and optional review scope, quiz title, and question formats. This module converts source material into a configured generation request.

screenshots.title: Generated study-set confirmation
screenshots.description: An uploaded file, selected formats, question count, and difficulty remain visible after the Study Set Ready confirmation. The completion message reports a generated set; the screenshot alone does not validate question quality.

screenshots.title: Saved quizzes and retakes
screenshots.description: The populated library distinguishes a new, untaken study set from a completed set with a score. Review Answers, Take Quiz, and Retake actions connect storage to practice and revision.

screenshots.title: Quiz session configuration
screenshots.description: Time-limit presets, question shuffle, and answer shuffle configure a selected quiz attempt. Start Quiz begins the session after the learner chooses how to practice.

screenshots.title: Active quiz question
screenshots.description: A question counter, elapsed time, progress bar, answer choices, and Next Question button show the testing interface. The learner selects an answer before advancing; this capture demonstrates layout rather than verified content accuracy.

screenshots.title: Results and answer review
screenshots.description: A completion score and duration appear above individual answer comparisons. Red and green review cards distinguish mistakes from correct responses, helping learners identify material to revisit.

screenshots.title: Flashcard study session
screenshots.description: A single card shows deck progress, mastery, flip interaction, audio/bookmark icons, and shuffle, hint, and star controls. This mode turns a saved study set into repeated recall practice.

screenshots.title: Nursing-review home
screenshots.description: Quick actions open the AI tutor, clinical cases, care plans, notes, anatomy lab, and practice quizzes. Nursing-practice sections continue below, making the home screen the starting point for different review activities.

screenshots.title: AI tutor conversation
screenshots.description: The chat screen shows a learner question, a generated explanation, a message field, and a clear-history action. It supports follow-up study questions; the visible response is AI-generated material, not validated clinical guidance.

screenshots.title: Clinical-case category selection
screenshots.description: Topic cards group practice around physiology, emergencies, disease, prioritization, pharmacology, and communication. Learners choose the area for a generated scenario rather than starting with an unrelated random case.

screenshots.title: Additional clinical-case topics
screenshots.description: The lower category list adds maternal/child care, ethics, diagnostics, infection control, and a random-topic option. It expands the same scenario-selection module to more review areas.

screenshots.title: Notes and journal
screenshots.description: A saved note card and New note button show the personal writing space. This module keeps short reflections, reminders, and study notes alongside the review tools.

screenshots.title: Anatomy topic library
screenshots.description: Illustrated cards organize labeling exercises by structure, including heart, neuron, skin, bone, eye, and respiratory topics. Each card identifies the body system and the number of parts available for practice.

screenshots.title: Heart-labeling exercise
screenshots.description: Numbered callouts connect a heart diagram to a list of labels, with some entries left for the learner to complete. Visible attribution identifies the illustration source; the activity focuses on recalling anatomical names.

screenshots.title: Practice-quiz topic browser
screenshots.description: Numbered subtopics and completion indicators sit under a nursing-practice section. Learners can see which topics remain unattempted and select material for a focused quiz.

screenshots.title: Question-type selection
screenshots.description: A bottom sheet lets the learner select multiple choice, identification, enumeration, and matching. The Start button reflects the chosen types before a practice attempt begins.

screenshots.title: Timed practice question
screenshots.description: A countdown, question number, point value, answer choices, and Next button form the quiz-taking view. The interface supports timed retrieval practice without requiring the learner to leave the selected topic.

screenshots.title: Quiz results and rationales
screenshots.description: The results page combines score, correct-answer count, points, and duration with question-by-question review. Rationale text and Retry help users revisit mistakes after an attempt.

screenshots.title: Study-module slide reader
screenshots.description: A paginated slide displays module notes with previous/next navigation. Ask AI and Quiz this subtopic connect reading to explanation and practice, keeping those activities tied to the current material.

screenshots.title: App launch identity
screenshots.description: The splash screen presents the Musikk mark and AI Stem Studio label before the main interface loads. It establishes the application identity without yet showing a processing or playback result.

screenshots.title: Repertoire and song preparation
screenshots.description: Upload, format filters, search, and collection tabs organize the song library. A saved track reports four stems ready and offers Load into Stems, linking processing status to the mixer.

screenshots.title: Instrument-channel mixer
screenshots.description: The stem screen combines shared transport, a multichannel waveform, and individual instrument strips with volume and solo controls. Audio is still initializing in this capture, so it demonstrates mixer controls rather than confirmed playback.

screenshots.title: Vocal-channel controls
screenshots.description: The vocals strip is visible above the drums strip, with a fader, numeric level, and solo/mute-style controls. Users can adjust a part independently when valid stem audio has been loaded.

screenshots.title: Playback effects panel
screenshots.description: The Effects tab reveals speed, pitch, and deep-filter controls underneath the shared waveform. These settings support slowing a passage or transposing playback for practice; the captured transport remains in its initializing state.

screenshots.title: Profile and processing allowance
screenshots.description: The profile shows account identity, remaining AI-processing minutes, upgrade cards, and processing-quality selection. It communicates usage and plan options; the visible prices do not establish a completed payment integration.

screenshots.title: Audio, storage, and account settings
screenshots.description: Profile rows lead to identity editing, processing quality, Firebase/storage information, privacy, and logout. The screen groups technical preferences and account actions below the plan presentation.

screenshots.title: Account onboarding
screenshots.description: A product introduction leads into Google sign-in or email/password account creation, with a marketing preference and terms links. This is the entry flow before building a repertoire and using the practice tools.

screenshots.title: JournalEase splash screen
screenshots.description: The owl-and-graduation-cap mark introduces the journal with its beige/brown visual theme. This is a startup identity screen, not a cloud-sync or authentication status display.

screenshots.title: Empty note library
screenshots.description: The note list is empty, with a search action, overflow menu, and prominent add button. It gives first-time users a direct route to creating their first entry.

screenshots.title: Note creation editor
screenshots.description: A title and body are being entered, with Clear Fields and save controls near the bottom. This module captures a new local journal entry before returning to the library.

screenshots.title: Saved note and confirmation
screenshots.description: A note card appears alongside a Note Created Successfully message. The card exposes an overflow menu for follow-up actions, confirming that the create flow has returned to the library.

screenshots.title: Multiple color-coded entries
screenshots.description: Two cards show how the collection grows, with distinct colors, title/body previews, and per-note menus. Users can scan the library and reopen an entry without viewing every note in full.

screenshots.title: Local demo sign-in
screenshots.description: Email/password fields, password visibility, recovery, and registration links form the login interface. The current repository uses a local demo session; this screen should not be interpreted as real account protection or cloud synchronization.

screenshots.title: RFID kiosk ready state
screenshots.description: The terminal displays Ready to Scan, a manual-entry shortcut, and a recent-attendance panel. This is the waiting state before an employee presents a registered RFID card.

screenshots.title: Employment-start validation
screenshots.description: A warning explains that the selected employee has not reached the scheduled employment start date. It shows how the attendance validator blocks a tap that falls before the permitted start date.

screenshots.title: Controlled date/time test tool
screenshots.description: The Time Changer dialog lets a tester select a date/time, preview it, apply an override, or clear it. It supports controlled attendance scenarios without presenting the override as a normal employee operation.

screenshots.title: Time-in confirmation
screenshots.description: The feedback screen identifies the employee, recorded time, department, role, and attendance status. The captured test displays an on-time result, giving the person immediate confirmation that the tap was recorded.

screenshots.title: Time-out confirmation
screenshots.description: The corresponding time-out screen shows the employee and the end-of-day tap result. It completes the visible attendance pair while keeping recorded time and status readable at the kiosk.

screenshots.title: Administrator sign-in
screenshots.description: A campus-branded login form overlays a photograph of STI College Santa Rosa. Email, password, and session options provide the entry point to the attendance-management dashboard.

screenshots.title: Dashboard overview
screenshots.description: The dashboard combines an institutional banner, employee/department counts, attendance summaries, and persistent navigation. It provides a starting overview before administrators open operational modules.

screenshots.title: Attendance monitoring
screenshots.description: Summary cards classify attendance while the log table shows employee, log type, time, date, and status. Search, date/department filters, and refresh controls help staff inspect individual tap records.

screenshots.title: Daily Time Record generation
screenshots.description: The DTR command center walks the user through cutoff selection, a faculty member, school year, and semester. Single-record generation and bulk-print actions turn attendance records into reporting output.

screenshots.title: Printable DTR preview
screenshots.description: A modal previews the faculty Daily Time Record in a page-oriented layout, with Close and Print DTR actions. Administrators can inspect the selected report before sending it to a printer.

screenshots.title: Teaching-schedule management
screenshots.description: Faculty cards summarize class counts by weekday under the active term. Search, department/status filters, and grid/list options help staff locate and manage teaching schedules; this capture shows an employee with no classes.

screenshots.title: Exam-schedule management
screenshots.description: The exam-schedule page provides staff search, filters, past-exam visibility, and grid/list views. Its No Teaching Staff Found state shows how the module handles a selection without available staff records.

screenshots.title: Employee directory and departments
screenshots.description: Search and employment filters sit above an employee table containing identity, department, contact, RFID/schedule, and work-status information. Add Employee and department-management controls maintain the records used by attendance and scheduling.

screenshots.title: Holiday and no-class setup
screenshots.description: The holiday module offers Add Holiday and an empty list for holidays, suspended classes, and no-class days. These entries provide scheduling exceptions that administrators can maintain as the calendar changes.

screenshots.title: Substitute assignments
screenshots.description: Search, status filtering, and refresh controls organize class-substitution requests. The empty state indicates no assignments are currently listed and directs staff toward creating a substitution.

screenshots.title: Substitution records and forms
screenshots.description: Date-range, schedule-type, and text filters narrow substitution records intended for review and printing. This capture shows no matching forms, distinguishing the reporting view from assignment creation.

screenshots.title: Attendance verification filings
screenshots.description: Leave-token limits and filing-status totals appear above verification records and search. The module supports reviewing employee attendance-related filings and their approval state; this capture contains zero totals.

screenshots.title: Activity log and audit trail
screenshots.description: Date, action, user-type, and text filters narrow a table of recorded actions such as login and record creation. Administrators can review who acted, when, and the logged description during investigation or support.

screenshots.title: Academic-term configuration
screenshots.description: The active-term summary and term table show academic year, semester, date boundaries, duration, and status. Add/edit controls organize the term context used by scheduling and reports.

screenshots.title: Database backup and restore
screenshots.description: Connection status and last-backup information appear above backup creation and restore controls. This is an administrative recovery module; the screenshot shows the interface, not a completed or verified restoration.

screenshots.title: Startup loading screen
screenshots.description: Pet Haven branding and a progress bar introduce the Windows application. This screen precedes account entry and the shop-management workspace.

screenshots.title: Staff login
screenshots.description: Username and password fields open the staff session. The split layout keeps shop branding beside the login form; the screenshot documents the interface rather than the strength of its authentication.

screenshots.title: Main workspace and daily sales
screenshots.description: Navigation provides access to dashboard, customer, employee, product, and billing modules. A daily-report area displays the current sales total and a reset action, giving staff a persistent operational summary.

screenshots.title: Inventory category summary
screenshots.description: Dog, cat, fish, and bird cards display category counts with a refresh control. This dashboard gives staff a quick view of the animal-category records represented in the inventory.

screenshots.title: Customer registration and editing
screenshots.description: A customer list sits behind a modal collecting name, address, and phone number. Save, Update, and Cancel support adding or revising customer records used by the sales workflow.

screenshots.title: Product registration and stock fields
screenshots.description: The product modal captures name, type, animal category, quantity, and price. Its actions maintain the inventory records that cashiers select during billing.

screenshots.title: Bill composition and checkout
screenshots.description: Selected products appear with quantity, unit price, line totals, and transaction number. Add Product, quantity controls, removal actions, and Check Out let the cashier assemble and review a sale.

screenshots.title: Daily total after a sale
screenshots.description: The billing list is empty while the daily-report total has increased compared with the previous capture. It illustrates the post-sale workspace and updated summary; a receipt document itself is not shown.

screenshots.title: Application startup
screenshots.description: A medical icon and loading bar introduce the desktop project before login. This is a startup presentation screen, not a patient or administrative record view.

screenshots.title: Administrator login
screenshots.description: The branded login window accepts a username and password before opening the management modules. It establishes the account-entry flow for the school-project hospital interface.

screenshots.title: Doctor record management
screenshots.description: Name, contact number, specialization, and account fields sit above a doctor table with record actions. Administrators use this module to maintain the doctor directory for related appointment workflows.

screenshots.title: Patient registration
screenshots.description: Demographic fields, diagnosis, and doctor assignment appear above the patient list. The module captures the patient information referenced by appointments and billing in the demonstration system.

screenshots.title: Appointment scheduling
screenshots.description: Patient and doctor selectors combine with appointment date, status, time fields, floor, and availability. A table below organizes saved appointments for administrative review.

screenshots.title: Medical billing and receipt actions
screenshots.description: The bill form connects a patient and diagnosis with medication, procedures, treatment costs, payment method, and totals. View Receipt, Pay, and Delete expose the billing actions; the capture does not show a completed payment or receipt.

screenshots.title: Brand story and positioning
screenshots.description: The About page combines a brand headline, supporting statement, illustration, and story text. It explains the label identity alongside the storefront instead of presenting only product listings.

screenshots.title: Editorial article listing
screenshots.description: Image-led article cards display titles, dates, excerpts, and Continue Reading links. The blog module provides style and brand content that complements the shopping pages.

screenshots.title: Contact and inquiry form
screenshots.description: An address and phone block sits beside name, email, subject, and message fields. Visitors can compose an inquiry through Send message; the screenshot does not demonstrate successful delivery.

screenshots.title: Storefront landing page
screenshots.description: A campaign photograph, headline, Shop the collection button, and story link introduce the label. The hero offers a direct path to products while keeping brand information accessible.

screenshots.title: Filtered product catalog
screenshots.description: Category, price, and size filters sit beside product cards with names, prices, stock badges, and bag controls. This shopping module helps customers narrow the catalog and inspect available pieces.

screenshots.title: Main menu
screenshots.description: The title screen presents Play and Quit over a red horror-themed background. It is the entry point that establishes the tone before the player starts a session.

screenshots.title: Exterior establishing cinematic
screenshots.description: A nighttime view of the school introduces the setting before exploration begins. The visible skip prompt lets the player move past the cinematic rather than replaying it on every run.

screenshots.title: Character close-up cinematic
screenshots.description: A close-up character shot continues the opening sequence, with the same skip prompt. It demonstrates the character presentation and cinematic framing used before first-person gameplay.

screenshots.title: Hooded-character cinematic
screenshots.description: A second character appears in a dim interior during the opening sequence. The shot builds scene context and atmosphere; the still image alone does not establish the character role or enemy behavior.

screenshots.title: Exploration, objectives, and HUD
screenshots.description: The first-person view shows a school interior, an Interact prompt, resource bars, and page collection at seven of eight. This is the active exploration module, where navigation, interactions, and the collection objective meet.

videos.title: Silid 1201 gameplay recording
videos.description: The original gameplay recording shows the opening cinematics and first-person exploration, including the school setting, character encounter, page objective, and on-screen resource indicators.

screenshots.title: All in Place live-event setup
screenshots.description: A laptop and projected display show the All in Place timer during an activity. The photograph documents the application in an event setting, with large digits visible beyond the operator screen.

screenshots.title: Chef Xpress elapsed-time display
screenshots.description: A venue laptop shows the Chef Xpress preset counting elapsed time. This photograph demonstrates how an organizer can place the timing interface at the activity site.

screenshots.title: Travelogue timer at an event
screenshots.description: The Travelogue preset is visible on a laptop during a presentation setting. The elapsed-time display gives the operator a reference for tracking how long a presentation has run.

screenshots.title: Event venue context
screenshots.description: The photograph shows contestants, judges, equipment, and the THM Week venue. It documents the environment associated with the timer project, rather than exposing a separate software module.

screenshots.title: Codefest long-duration countdown
screenshots.description: The Codefest preset opens at 36 hours with Start, Reset, and keyboard hints. It adapts the countdown module to a long coding competition while keeping the display readable at a distance.

screenshots.title: Essay contest countdown
screenshots.description: The Essay Does It preset starts from one hour and shares the countdown controls. Event artwork identifies the contest while the timer gives participants a common deadline.

screenshots.title: Mix N Flair stopwatch
screenshots.description: The elapsed-time preset starts at zero, with Start and Reset controls. It records duration instead of counting down from a fixed limit, suiting activities measured by time taken.

screenshots.title: Preparation and speech phases
screenshots.description: Stand Up and Deliver shows a preparation countdown, separate prep/speech duration settings, and a skip-preparation option. This module supports moving between the two stages of a speaking activity.

screenshots.title: Think Quest question timer
screenshots.description: Easy, Medium, and Hard choices expose 15-, 30-, and 45-second limits above a large countdown. The quiz timer lets the host select a duration appropriate to the current round.

screenshots.title: Travelogue stopwatch preset
screenshots.description: The Travelogue interface begins at zero with elapsed-time labeling and standard timer controls. It reuses the stopwatch behavior with presentation-specific branding.

screenshots.title: Worth the Whisk countdown
screenshots.description: The cooking/baking preset opens at three hours with Start, Reset, and keyboard shortcuts. It applies the countdown module to a longer practical contest.

additionalScreenshots.title: Contest-preset launcher
additionalScreenshots.description: The launcher presents the available college contest presets as large illustrated choices. Operators can open a timer matched to the activity without configuring every screen from scratch.

additionalScreenshots.title: Event branding display
additionalScreenshots.description: A full-screen STI logo provides a branded holding display between timed activities. This screen presents event identity rather than an active countdown.

additionalScreenshots.title: All in Place countdown
additionalScreenshots.description: The All in Place preset opens with a 30-minute countdown, Start and Reset controls, and keyboard shortcuts. It gives this contest a fixed-duration timing display.

additionalScreenshots.title: Chef Xpress stopwatch
additionalScreenshots.description: The Chef Xpress preset counts elapsed time from zero, with standard start/pause and reset actions. Contest-specific artwork distinguishes it from the other stopwatch modes.

videos.title: STITimer screenshot walkthrough
videos.description: A silent, captioned walkthrough of the existing event photos and timer screenshots. It explains live-event context, countdowns, stopwatch presets, speech phases, and quiz timing. This is a still-image presentation, not a recording of live timer interaction.

screenshots.title: Conversion request setup
screenshots.description: The form accepts a YouTube link, individual/playlist mode, output format, and audio quality. Fetch Metadata begins the preview stage, while an adjacent guide explains the conversion flow.

screenshots.title: Metadata preview and confirmation
screenshots.description: The retrieved thumbnail, title, and channel let users check the source before conversion. The preview panel provides Back and Convert now actions while retaining the selected output options.

screenshots.title: Completed conversion and download
screenshots.description: The result panel reports a ready download with format and file size. Download File, Copy link, and Convert another connect the completed background job to retrieval and the next request.
